title: DynamoLLM: Designing LLM Inference Clusters for Performance and Energy Efficiency
technique: Hierarchical controllers reconfigure per-request-type instance pools (count, tensor parallelism, GPU frequency) using energy-performance profiles to minimize energy under TTFT/TBT SLOs

optimized_metrics.evidence: The optimization target of the solver is to minimize the total energy consumption (E)
we assume an SLO such that the P99 tail latency is within 5× of the execution time of a request on an unloaded system
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: P99 tail latency is within 5× of the execution time of a request on an unloaded system

optimized_metrics.evidence: We define SLOs for TTFT and TBT based on maximum achievable performance, described in Table IV. ... We set the SLOs to 5× the latency of a single request running isolated on a system
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: we assume an SLO such that the P99 tail latency is within 5× of the execution time of a request on an unloaded system

optimized_metrics.evidence: DynamoLLM automatically and dynamically reconfigures the inference cluster to optimize for energy and cost of LLM serving under the service's performance SLOs.

headline_claim.text: at a service-level, DynamoLLM conserves 53% energy and 38% operational carbon emissions, and reduces 61% cost to the customer, while meeting the latency SLOs.

reported_metrics.where: §VI latency comparison (P50 and P99 TTFT/TBT vs SinglePool)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: TTFT is the latency of generating the first output token; while TBT is the latency to generate each new output token.
metric_definitions.notes: TBT here is per-new-token latency; queueing inclusion not stated

metric_definitions.definition_quote: To quantify the energy efficiency, we measure the energy consumption in Watt-hours (Wh) while meeting certain latency SLOs.
metric_definitions.notes: absolute Wh over an experiment, not Wh per token

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We set the SLOs to 5× the latency of a single request running isolated on a system [30].
metric_definitions.notes: SLO = 5x unloaded latency for TTFT and TBT per request-length bucket (Table IV); relaxed services 10x or 20x; evaluated at P99

slo_spec: TTFT and TBT SLOs per 9 request-length buckets (SS..LL; thresholds at 33rd/66th/100th percentile of Azure Conversation trace lengths), set to 5x the isolated single-request latency, P99 tail within SLO; looser 10x/20x discussed
load_regime: trace replay (Azure Conversation and Coding week-long traces; 1-hour open-source traces) plus Poisson Low/Medium/High load sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Energy-vs-latency: DynamoLLM raises P50 TTFT and TBT by 11.4% and 7.6% over SinglePool while reducing P99 TTFT/TBT by 5.3% and 11.1% (text as written); savings shrink at higher load (51% / 40% / 23.4% at low/medium/high); reconfiguration overheads
hardware: NVIDIA DGX H100 servers (profiling and experiments); cluster-scale simulation
workloads: Azure LLM inference traces (Conversation, Coding), open-source production traces
extractor_notes: Energy is the objective, latency only a constraint (SLO stated as P99 within 5x unloaded execution time). Fig 7 text: the P99 TTFT/TBT reduction (5.3%/11.1%) and P50 increase (11.4%/7.6%) are relative to SinglePool. Energy unit is Wh over an experiment window, not per token.

tail_audit.metrics: TTFT, TBT @ P99 within 5x isolated latency
